summary: Deborah and Barak sing a song of praise because Israel is delivered from Canaanite bondage.
meta_description: Deborah and Barak sing a song of praise because Israel is delivered from Canaanite bondage.

footnotes.note10_a: IE on animals used by rich merchants, leaders.
footnotes.note10_b: Hebrew meaning uncertain; perhaps “on rich cloths, carpets.”
footnotes.note11_a: HEB By the voices of archers down among the watering places, there they rehearse the righteousness of Jehovah, even the righteousness of His rulers in Israel. Then the people of the Lord went down to the gates.
footnotes.note13_a: HEB Then a remnant descended against the nobles; the people of the Lord descended for me against the mighty.
footnotes.note14_b: HEB hold the sceptre of the muster-officer, the marshal’s staff.
footnotes.note22_a: OR Then did the horse hooves stamp.
footnotes.note30_a: HEB Are they not finding, dividing spoil?
footnotes.note30_b: OR a spoil of dyed stuffs.
